evidence_items.locator: Key findings, Assessment has changed substantially
evidence_items.explanation: This is strong evidence of perceived assessment changes among surveyed UK undergraduates. The survey was conducted before the post, so its later publication does not make it evidence of subsequent forecast fulfillment.

evidence_items.locator: AI Frees Up Time for What Matters Most to Educators
evidence_items.explanation: The survey reports AI use by 59% of US K–12 educators during the 2025–2026 school year and perceived time savings among most users. This supports meaningful effects on educators' work, but does not establish their magnitude or changes in classroom practice.

The February–March teacher survey indicates that formal institutional responses remain limited. This constrains claims of comprehensive institutional transformation, although informal disruption could itself constitute a large impact.
